Definition: Product-owned component that owns the harness turn lifecycle behavior.
Notes: Routes stay thin; engine owns lifecycle

Definition: Product-owned boundary for turn execution, UI events, canonical HarnessEvents, interrupt behavior, and terminal outcomes.
Chirality-owned canonical runtime event persisted in append-only JSONL; versioned shape with schemaVersion, eventId, sessionId, timestamp, type, data.
Compact browser-facing event mapped from terminal runtime signals; names must remain Chirality-owned and SSE-compatible.
Browser-facing SSE event; an interrupted process:exit is the required symptom of an active-turn interrupt.
Persisted acceptance record written before model/provider execution as the recovery anchor.
SPEC/TYPES terminal event category; candidate carrier for interruption via reason metadata.
Proposed separate terminal event type for interruption; not in current SPEC/TYPES initial categories.
Status returned when a concurrent turn attempt is made for a session that already has an active turn.
Public route that interrupts the active turn and aborts the active provider request.
Route that executes a turn and streams browser-facing UI events over SSE; acts as a thin transport adapter.
Durable success, failure, cancellation, or interruption result that every accepted turn must reach.
Per-session liveness state that must be released across all terminal paths.
Append-only newline-delimited JSONL audit mirror at .chirality/sessions/<id>/events.jsonl; canonical runtime audit record.
Small deterministic component mapping completion, failure, cancellation, and interruption signals into UIEvents and HarnessEvents.
Transport-level loss of the SSE client; triggers cleanup and cancellation recording but is not necessarily explicit user intent to interrupt.
Requirement that API keys and provider secrets are excluded from terminal events, logs, provider errors, and tool artifacts.
